title: Upper limb · Persian Group A · 1403/10/9
note: TUMS Persian-language Group A, cover dated 1403/10/9. Twenty questions translated from the original. Handwritten circles are not an authenticated key.

questions.prompt: Which statement about carpal bones is incorrect?
options: Trapezium is most lateral distal-row bone
Lunate is the conventional commonly dislocated carpal
Pisiform is first carpal to ossify
questions.note: Pisiform ossifies last; capitate generally first.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All bound the axillary apex EXCEPT:
questions.note: Cervicoaxillary canal is bounded by rib, scapula and clavicle.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which does not attach to medial scapular border?
questions.note: Teres minor arises from lateral border.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which lies posterior to third part of axillary artery?
questions.note: Radial nerve lies posteriorly; posterior cord is more proximal behind second part.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Deltoid paralysis chiefly impairs arm abduction through:
questions.note: The conventional functional range for deltoid is 15–90 degrees, with overlapping muscle contributions.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Bicipital aponeurosis passes obliquely deep to which structure?
questions.note: It separates superficial vein from artery and median nerve below.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All relate to separation of medial and lateral triceps heads EXCEPT:
questions.note: Radial nerve and profunda traverse radial groove; radial artery is in forearm.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All muscles attached around intertubercular groove perform:
questions.note: Pectoralis major, latissimus and teres major medially rotate.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Suprascapular-nerve injury impairs which movements?
questions.note: Supraspinatus abducts; infraspinatus laterally rotates. The handwritten D is not adopted.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which does not form a boundary of triangle of auscultation?
questions.note: Rhomboid is part of the floor, not a named boundary.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All are rotator-cuff muscles EXCEPT:
questions.note: Teres minor, not teres major, is a cuff muscle.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Thoracodorsal artery branches from:
questions.note: Thoracodorsal is a major subscapular branch.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Little-finger lymph drains most directly toward which axillary group?
questions.note: Medial upper-limb lymph generally follows basilic pathway toward humeral/lateral nodes, often via cubital nodes.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which nerve–muscle passage pairing is incorrect?
questions.note: Radial artery, not radial nerve, passes between first dorsal interosseous heads.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All pass superficially over flexor retinaculum EXCEPT:
questions.note: Superficial radial nerve passes dorsolaterally rather than across palmar retinaculum.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which median-nerve statement is false?
options: It crosses brachial artery lateral to medial
questions.note: Anterior forearm skin uses medial/lateral antebrachial cutaneous nerves; median cutaneous territory is hand.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which superficial-palmar-arch statement is false?
options: It is formed mainly by superficial ulnar branch
It is proximal to deep palmar arch
It is deep to palmar aponeurosis
It is superficial to FDS/FDP tendons
questions.note: Superficial arch lies distal to deep arch.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which movement is relatively spared by ulnar-nerve injury?
questions.note: Opponens pollicis is chiefly median supplied; adductor/hypothenar actions are ulnar.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: Which brachioradialis statement is incorrect?
options: It flexes elbow although grouped with posterior forearm muscles
It originates on lateral humeral epicondyle
It flexes elbow and is radial supplied
Radial artery lies deep to it in anterior forearm
questions.note: Origin is lateral supracondylar ridge, not common epicondylar extensor origin.
questions.subject: anatomy

questions.prompt: All three brachial-plexus cords can contribute to which glenohumeral movement?
questions.note: Flexion recruits anterior deltoid (posterior cord), biceps/coracobrachialis (lateral) and pectoralis major (medial/lateral pectoral).
questions.subject: anatomy

audit.method: Source photograph transcription; anatomy review; original defects preserved, multiple defensible choices accepted.
